entries.title: Opening a shop of your own
q: how do i open a shop
how do i make a shop
can i have my own shop
how to set up a store
how do i sell things in my own shop
how to make a shop in the village
how do i run a shop
entries.answer: Press U → Open a shop. It's the easiest business: a building with a Shop Counter, a door onto a street and a chest of stock. You fill the shelves, folk come in and buy at the counter, the coin goes into its till. No charter and no hands to pay; just a licence when you register.
steps: Press U → Open a shop: choose premises (a building of your own, have the town build it, or buy one for sale).
Building your own: any room with walls, a roof and a door onto a street or the square; set a Shop Counter in it (or hang a Shop Sign).
The shop's screen opens on Setup: name it, pick its kind and hours, and register (a licence of a week's rates, 3 coins at least).
Stock it: every chest, barrel, shelf and pot inside is stock. Set prices on Stock & prices.
Follow 'Getting started' on the Shop tab until the first sale.
controls: [Right-click] Shop Counter → Setup · Stock & prices · Books · Keeper
tips: Stock what folk here have a use for: the Stock tab says who would buy each ware and why.
One shop per town. A shop wants no standing, unlike a chartered business.
warn: Until the checklist is all ticks it stays shut: its sign says what it still needs.

entries.title: What a shop needs (the checklist)
q: no path from the door to a street
entries.answer: A shop opens only when everything is ticked: a counter, walls and a roof (the room is filled out from the counter, so a gap shows), a door, the door reached from a street or the square, a chest/barrel/shelf/pot of stock (not all back stock), ground a building may stand on (not a street or the mine), and its kind's kit (a bakery an oven, a butcher a smoker or oven, a tool shop an anvil or furnace, a clothier a loom, an apothecary a brewing stand, a tavern two seats).
steps: Open the shop's screen: each line is a tick or a cross with where to get it.
Fix the crosses; a line over the hotbar reminds you while you build nearby.
When it's complete you're told 'Your shop is ready to open!'
controls: [Right-click] Shop Counter → Shop tab → Getting started
tips: A door below the floor, or a blocked way out, fails 'reached from a street': the message names the door.

entries.title: Stocking a shop and setting prices
q: how do i set prices in my shop
how do i stock my shop
what should i sell in my shop
what do folk want to buy
entries.answer: Every chest, barrel, shelf and pot inside the shop is stock. On Stock & prices, each ware has its price for a lot with − and + (Shift for ten), Going price and Keep back, how folk will take your price, and who would buy it and why. Mark containers as back stock to hide them from customers (a keeper restocks from them).
steps: Put wares in the shop's chests.
Open Stock & prices and set each price (or press Going price).
Read the top line: how many wares have buyers in town, and what folk here want.
Restock what sells; drop what nobody has a use for.
tips: Folk buy only what they have a real use for now: their trade's tool, food for the household, a remedy, seed, a piece for the home.
Fair prices and full shelves raise the shop's name; dear prices and bare shelves lower it.

entries.title: Hiring a shopkeeper
q: can i hire someone to run my shop
how do i hire a keeper
who runs my shop when im away
entries.answer: The Keeper tab lists folk who can be spared and their wage. Taken on, a keeper stands behind your counter in its hours, greets customers and fills the shelves from the back stock. It's paid its day's wage from the till each morning; the tab sets the wage against what the till takes a day.
warn: A keeper goes after two days' wages owed. Stock what sells first if the wage is more than the shop takes.

entries.title: Shop Sign
q: do i need a shop sign
entries.answer: Hang a Shop Sign on the wall of a room to mark it as your shop (instead of setting a counter); it opens the shop's screen. Craft it from 2 planks and a sign. A shop still needs a counter for customers to pay at.

entries.title: Starting a business (a charter)
q: how do i start a business
how do i make a business
how much does a business cost
entries.answer: Press U → Start a business (or ask any folk 'I'd like to start a business', or the bank's counter): three steps with the best already chosen, so Next, Next, Confirm works. 1. A kind (what the town is short of first, with the week's takings to expect). 2. Premises (your shop, a stall or a room the town lets, have the town build it, or buy a building). 3. Confirm: the charter fee (10 coins) and the building, with 'Borrow N and open it' if you're short.
steps: U → Start a business → 1. A kind: pick (the first is 'A shop of your own, the easiest').
2. Premises: choose one; for a new building, pick a drawing and a plot from the gallery.
3. Confirm and open it.
Then follow the welcome's next steps and run it from Your businesses.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Trade → Money → Start a business
tips: A chartered firm has hands of its own who make and sell its wares.
The town charters anybody it knows and has nothing against: a citizen, a friend, or a visitor who has said hello.
warn: A stranger nobody has spoken to is turned away: say hello to a few folk first (the step offers a button).

entries.title: Running your businesses
q: how do i run my business
how do i pay my workers
entries.answer: Your businesses (U → Run it, or 'Show me my businesses') runs a firm by tabs: Summary, Hands (the best the town can spare, post an opening, take the best applicant), Stock (order its makings), Prices (its markup beside the going price), Money (invest, take drawings) and Shares & closing (the bourse, winding it up).
controls: Tabs: Summary · Hands · Stock · Prices · Money · Shares & closing
tips: A new player's firm has a week's grace; if it's in trouble you're told daily in chat what to do (coin in the till, stock, a hand).
warn: A firm owing more than it's worth, out of cash and credit, can be taken to court by its creditors after the grace.

entries.title: Every kind of business
q: what kinds of business are there
entries.answer: Makers: toolsmith, armourer, carpenter, clothier, weaver, chandler, potter, glassworks. Food and drink: baker, butcher, fishmonger, café, tavern, inn, apothecary. Shops: greengrocer, general store, stationer. Each wants a certain age and size of town, and a stall on the square or a room the town lets in its trade's building.
steps: U → Start a business: the kinds the town can have are listed, best for you first, with the reason and expected takings.
Pick one the town is short of (marked 'wanted').
tips: Wood Age kinds: toolsmith, carpenter, clothier, weaver, baker, fishmonger, greengrocer. Stone Age adds chandler, potter, glassworks, butcher, café, tavern, general store. Iron Age adds armourer, inn, apothecary, stationer.
The greengrocer and general store buy in at the market and sell on; the rest make what they sell.

entries.title: The makers: tools, armour, furniture, cloth, candles, pots, glass
entries.answer: Toolsmith (stone and iron tools, shears, buckets; a stall; Wood Age, 10 folk). Armourer (iron armour, shields, swords; a room; Iron Age, 18). Carpenter (chests, barrels, beds, tables, frames, ladders; Wood, 10). Clothier (leather clothes; Wood, 12). Weaver (wool, rugs, banners; Wood, 12). Chandler (candles, honey, comb; Stone, 12). Potter (pots, bricks, terracotta; Stone, 12). Glassworks (glass, panes, bottles; a room; Stone, 14).

entries.title: Food and drink: bakery, butcher, fish, café, tavern, inn, apothecary
entries.answer: Baker (bread, cake, cookies, pies; Wood Age, 8 folk). Butcher (cooked meats; Stone, 10). Fishmonger (raw and cooked fish, its own catch; Wood, 8). Café (stews, soups, baked potatoes; a room; Stone, 14). Tavern (every café drink; a room; Stone, 14). Inn (hearty meals; a room; Iron, 30). Apothecary (potions, bottles, glistering melon; Iron, 20).
tips: A café, tavern and inn start with hands besides their founder.

entries.title: Shops: greengrocer, general store, stationer
q: what does a general store sell
entries.answer: Greengrocer (carrots, potatoes, apples, beetroot, melon, berries; a stall; Wood Age, 12 folk) and General store (torches, lanterns, buckets, shears, flint and steel, rods; a room; Stone, 16) buy in at the market and sell on. Stationer (paper, books, maps; Iron, 20) makes its own.

entries.title: Premises: a stall, a room, or a building
q: what premises does a business need
have the town build my shop
buy a building for my business
rent a room for my business
entries.answer: A business works from your own shop (checked against its kind), a stall on the square (its own once paid for), a room the town lets in its trade's building (a weekly rent), a building the town builds you (a gallery of drawings with quotes, times and a plot), or a building bought on the property market.
tips: A firm that does well takes larger premises.
A firm on your own shop pays the town no rent.

entries.title: Renting a market stall
q: how do i rent a stall
entries.answer: Ask any folk 'Rent a stall' (Trade → Money), or right-click an empty stall on the square ('Stall to let'). A week's rent goes to the treasury (more in a bigger town; pay up to four weeks ahead). Stock its barrel, set prices on its screen, and folk buy from it with their own coin into its till.
steps: Rent it: Trade → Money → Rent a stall, or right-click a stall to let.
Right-click its barrel and put in what you'd sell.
Crouch and right-click the barrel (or right-click its sign) for the stall screen: a price box per ware beside the going price, and how folk will take it.
Take the till on the screen whenever you like.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Trade → Money → Rent a stall
tips: Market day brings nearly everybody with coin to look.
Rent run out? It shuts; three days on it's given back, your goods and till kept for you. Nothing is ever lost.

entries.title: Service counters: buying at the shop, café, tavern, bank, smithy
q: how do i buy from the town shop
how do i buy food from the cafe
entries.answer: Right-click a service point (the counter, or the keeper with coin in hand) for its screen: the keeper, hours, open or shut, your standing and coin. At a shop: goods by kind with prices and why they move, Order what's not in, a basket with − and +, discounts, and Buy; Sell lists what the town buys from you.
steps: Find the counter: shop and store 7am-7pm, café 6:30am-8pm, tavern 4:30pm-1:30am, bank 7:30am-5:30pm, smithy and tailor 7am-6pm.
Right-click it; add to the basket and press Buy (B).
Or use Sell, Order, or the trade's own panel (mend, made to order, deposit...).
tips: Discounts: a friend, a citizen, a haggle or a medal; unwelcome players pay double.
The service counter block is three slabs over a barrel between two planks.

entries.title: A business's books
q: how do i see a business's profit
entries.answer: A business's books show its owner and hands and their pay; today, this week and all time (takings, costs, wages, rent, taxes, net profit, drawings); a fourteen-day chart; what it sold item by item and how each is made; its stock; what it bought; and why its prices moved. The Businesses page lists every firm in town, a click to its books.
controls: [Right-click] an owner → Trade → Money → The books
tips: A business's books have a Buy button to make an offer for it.

entries.title: Folk's own businesses and competition
q: will folk compete with my shop
entries.answer: Folk open businesses of their own too, of the same kinds, when the town is short of something. They compete on price and name: a folk buying its needs goes to whichever seller is the better buy (price, the walk, the shop's name), including your shop.

entries.title: Opening Ribbon
q: how do i cut a ribbon
entries.answer: String an Opening Ribbon across a new doorway and cut it with shears: it snips in two and the folk about give a cheer. Craft three from two string and a red dye. A town's own ribbon across a great work is its leader's to cut at the opening.
